acceptanceCriteria: A simulated suspend gap is recorded once.
Idle and wall caps do not fire because of the gap.
Lease expiry during the gap does not reap a live worker.
Keep-awake is off by default and documented as not preventing lid-close sleep.
body: From GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#1040 (opened 2026-10-17). Feature request; not yet specified. Problem When the host suspends (lid closed, maintenance sleep) wall-clock timers keep counting: leases expire, idle or wall caps fire, and sleeping workers look hung, so work stalls or is killed on wake for no real reason. Nothing reports the suspend. Current workaround A doctor script reads kernel sleep/wake times and flags recent sleep; context tools subtract slept time; supervisor shells hold an idle-sleep assertion, which does not stop lid-close sleep. Proposal Detect suspend gaps (a large jump between wall and monotonic time across ticks) and record a `host-slept` event with its duration. Exclude the gap from idle and wall accounting, and give live leases a one-time extension bounded by the gap. Add a doctor finding. Optionally, `service install --keep-awake` holds an idle-sleep assertion while the service runs. See beamfall/corvint#1040 for the full text.
title: host sleep awareness for leases, idle and wall-clock caps (issue #1040)
